note: Capability families abstract public tool documentation; confirm actual tools/provider and current availability at runtime. Families 1-10 derive from the REA capability review; 'dart_aot_snapshot_analysis' derives from targeted community tooling research (blutter / reFlutter / Doldrums, web-verified 2026-10-13, see sources.md) and is not part of REA's published tool list.

observations: Dart SDK version is auto-detected from libflutter.so and a matching Dart runtime is compiled to parse libapp.so (blutter)
class hierarchy, method lists and annotated ARM64 assembly are recovered from the Dart AOT snapshot
the Dart object pool is dumped wholesale (pp.txt), exposing strings, constants and embedded endpoints or key material
an auto-generated Frida hook template (blutter_frida.js) attaches to recovered Dart functions
a patched Flutter engine can dump runtime snapshot state and neutralize BoringSSL certificate verification (reFlutter)
Dart 2.x-era snapshots are parsed by pure-Python tooling without compiling the runtime (Doldrums)
potential_exposures: licensing or authorization logic shipped inside libapp.so is recoverable as class/method structure
hard-coded endpoints, secrets and key material sit in the Dart object pool and are dumped in one pass
Flutter bypasses the platform TLS stack, so engine patching enables traffic interception
single-layer platform shrinkers (R8/ProGuard) touch only the Java/Kotlin host layer and leave the Dart snapshot intact
defense_options: enable Flutter release obfuscation (--obfuscate plus --split-debug-info) as a cost-raising baseline, not as a secret boundary
move final authorization decisions and durable secrets to a server or trusted boundary whenever the deployment posture allows
relocate critical pure functions behind an FFI boundary into a natively protected library so a different toolchain is required
admit Dart-aware virtualization candidates only after source-level verification of claims, license and maintenance
run the same analyst tooling against the own release artifact before distribution and record what is recovered
verification: run blutter-class tooling against the release libapp.so and record which classes and functions are recovered
confirm the object pool dump contains no secret or endpoint that requires protection
test the release build against engine patching (reFlutter) and Frida hooking attempts
differential and regression tests for FFI boundaries and the licensing flows
limitations: snapshot parsing depends on matching the exact Dart SDK version; tooling may lag new releases
obfuscated snapshots remain structurally parseable even though automated recovery of many functions degrades (the tool's own TODO tracks this)
a result on one arm64 Android build does not cover other ABIs, iOS builds or custom engine builds
community tooling evolves fast; re-verify every claim before relying on it
